rounds.text: Creative Newtech Ltd is demonstrating exceptional fundamental momentum that substantially outpaces its broader sector, evidenced by a rules-based screen scoring 96 out of 100 with a high-confidence BUY rating [E60]. The company has delivered a stellar compounded profit growth of 45% over five years alongside a 39% compounded sales growth over the same period [E14, E17], significantly outperforming sector medians of 17.1% and 11.8% respectively [E68, E69]. Profitability metrics similarly shine with a return on capital employed of 14.89% to 18.8% beating the sector benchmark of 6.5% [E10, E12], while return on equity stands at a robust 18.8% to 19.33% against a meager sector benchmark of 4.8% [E9, E13]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model suggests significant mispricing by offering a substantial margin of safety of 46.9% at the current market price [E43], supported by positive institutional money flow [E41] and a sector operating in a clear tailwind [E67]. Conceded: operating cash flow turned negative at minus 272 crore rupees in March 2026 alongside an increase in debtor days [E31, E58].

Creative Newtech Ltd carries significant financial and operational risks that are obscured by headline growth figures. Most critically, the business experienced a catastrophic collapse in cash generation, with operating cash flow plunging to negative Rs 272 Cr and free cash flow dropping to negative Rs 275 Cr in March 2026, resulting in a disastrous cash conversion ratio of -3.89x [E30, E31, E32]. This severe cash burn coincided with a massive surge in borrowings, which more than quadrupled from Rs 72 Cr to Rs 324 Cr in a single year [E36], pushing debt-to-equity to a moderate-to-risky 0.89x [E34]. Operational friction is clearly mounting as debtor days have deteriorated sharply from 52.0 to 76.3 days [E58]. Valuation multiples also reflect considerable downside risk, with P/E at 22.82x [E6], P/B at 4.62x [E7], and EV/EBITDA at 17.4x [E11], all trading at a heavy premium to their respective sector benchmarks of 18.87x, 1.51x, and 11.32x. Conceded: the company has delivered strong multi-year profit and sales growth alongside high historical returns on equity [E13, E17, E20]. However, insider alignment is weakening as promoter holding has decreased by 6.86% over the last 3 years [E59], and the stock carries extreme historical volatility of 52.7% alongside a peak-to-peak drawdown risk of -51.3% [E50, E51].

Conceded: operating cash flow dropped to negative Rs 272 Cr and free cash flow to negative Rs 275 Cr in March 2026 [E31, E32]. Conceded: borrowings rose from Rs 72 Cr to Rs 324 Cr in March 2026 [E36], pushing debt-to-equity to 0.89x [E34], and debtor days increased to 76.3 days [E58]. However, these short-term figures are heavily outweighed by elite multi-year compounding, including a 5-year sales growth of 39% and a 5-year profit growth of 45% [E14, E17]. Valuation premiums in P/E, P/B, and EV/EBITDA are entirely justified by exceptional capital efficiency metrics, led by an ROE of 18.8% and ROCE of 14.89% or 18.8%, vastly outperforming sector benchmarks [E6, E7, E8, E10, E11, E12, E13]. Furthermore, institutional money flow reads positive with institutional holdings expanding, pointing to smart-money backing despite promoter holding shifts [E38, E39, E40, E41, E59]. Finally, rules-based algorithmic screening scores the company at a high confidence 96 out of 100, and a DCF intrinsic valuation of Rs 2012 provides a massive 46.9% margin of safety against the current market price [E42, E43, E60].

Conceded: multi-year sales and profit growth figures are strong [E14, E17], and the rules-based screen scores 96 out of 100 [E60]. However, those historical achievements obscure a catastrophic collapse in liquidity, marked by operating cash flow plummeting to negative Rs 272 Cr and free cash flow hitting negative Rs 275 Cr in March 2026 [E31, E32], creating a cash conversion ratio of -3.89x [E30]. To fund this shortfall, borrowings quadrupled from Rs 72 Cr to Rs 324 Cr in a single year [E36], and debtor days deteriorated sharply from 52.0 to 76.3 days [E58], exposing severe working capital degradation that contradicts the idea of sustainable compounding. Furthermore, the claim of smart-money backing ignores the structural dilution by insiders, as promoter holdings have dropped by 6.86% over the last 3 years [E59]. Finally, valuation multiples trade at steep premiums to sector benchmarks, with EV/EBITDA at 17.4x versus the 11.32x sector median and P/B at 4.62x versus 1.51x [E7, E11], exposing investors to severe downside risk given a historical peak-to-trough drawdown of -51.3% and 52.7% annualised volatility [E50, E51].

Conceded: operating cash flow dropped to negative Rs 272 Cr and free cash flow hit negative Rs 275 Cr in March 2026 [E31, E32], borrowings rose to Rs 324 Cr [E36], and promoter holding decreased over 3 years [E59]. Despite those cash-flow pressures, the underlying business quality remains superior to the sector, boasting an ROA of 7.86% versus the 2.18% sector benchmark and an ROCE of 14.89% against 6.5% [E8, E10]. That operational efficiency underpins a rules-based screen scoring a high-confidence 96 out of 100 [E60], driven by robust top-line momentum including a 49% trailing twelve-month sales growth rate [E16]. Furthermore, the valuation premium is fully justified by exceptional financial outperformance where 5-year profit growth of 45% significantly outpaces the sector median of 17.1% [E17, E68]. Finally, institutional money flow is positive with foreign and domestic holdings both increasing since September 2023 [E39, E40, E41], validating market support despite historical volatility.

Conceded: ROA of 7.86% versus the 2.18% sector benchmark and ROCE of 14.89% against 6.5% [E8, E10], and that institutional holdings have increased since September 2023 [E39, E40, E41]. However, citing high operational efficiency and a rules-based screen score of 96 out of 100 [E60] ignores the severe deterioration in cash generation where operating cash flow collapsed to negative Rs 272 Cr and free cash flow hit negative Rs 275 Cr in March 2026 [E31, E32]. While trailing twelve-month sales growth reached 49% [E16], this top-line expansion has coincided with a sharp jump in borrowings to Rs 324 Cr from Rs 72 Cr a year earlier [E36] and a lengthening of debtor days from 52.0 to 76.3 days [E58]. Furthermore, the bull's reliance on 5-year profit growth of 45% [E17] masks a more recent vulnerability where price growth recently exceeded profit growth by 33%, signaling that market expectations are running dangerously ahead of actual delivery [E54]. Finally, pointing to a high screen score [E60] and positive institutional flows [E41] does not excuse structural insider dilution, evidenced by promoter holding decreasing over the last three years by 6.86% [E59].
